title: Fire safety in homes and commercial premises: electrical and cooking fires, and battery risks
asked: Ms Cassandra Lee asked what proportion of fires over the past three years came from electrical sources and cooking in homes and commercial premises, how many involved Fire Code breaches or non-compliant batteries, and what plans the Ministry has to strengthen fire safety frameworks and enforcement.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming gave the shares of fires from unattended cooking or electrical origin: 68%, 65% and 59% in residential premises and 66%, 72% and 67% in commercial premises from 2023 to 2025. Five residential fires and 11 commercial fires involved Fire Code breaches. SCDF does not track whether batteries involved in fires met regulatory requirements, and he pointed to MHA's response to the Adjournment Motion on "Fire Safety in Our Homes" on 12 January 2026. In his supplementary reply he said power banks are not tracked, but AMD batteries are, that AMD fires are under 5% of all fires with disproportionately higher injuries and fatalities, and that MHA and SCDF work with the People's Association, schools and Town Councils on outreach, enforcement and regulation.
